purpose: Direct-source analytical extraction from licensed IEEE primary texts supplied for EXTREQ-02. Clause identities and normative posture are preserved; summaries are VIGIL abstractions and licensed text is not reproduced.

source_scope_updates.extraction_scope_notes: Governance-relevant mandatory process outcomes and activities in Clauses 7 through 11 were decomposed, with bounded supporting recommendations retained where they materially qualify the process model.
Clause 5 stakeholder-specific transparency requirements and their progressive or non-progressive level conditions were decomposed from the primary text.

The source is primarily ontological rather than a process-control standard. Governance-relevant source-defined ontology domains and relationships were represented as definitional records without inventing operational duties.
Clauses 6 through 9 and the existing sixteen Annex A.3 baseline ASOI requirements were decomposed without duplicating or renumbering the existing Annex A.3 records.
The five well-being impact-assessment activities and governance-relevant recommended tasks in Clause 4 were decomposed with their recommended-practice posture preserved.
Governance-relevant mandatory and recommended life-cycle activities in Clause 4 were decomposed while retaining emulated-empathy-specific terminology and qualifications.

The recommended practices in Clause 6 were decomposed into bounded governance duties, preserving partner-based GPAI, emulated-empathy, dependency, autonomy, disclosure and relational-safeguard distinctions.

review_limitations: The extraction represents governance-relevant process duties and outcomes; informative annex material is not exhaustively atomised.
Licensed IEEE text is not stored in VIGIL.

requirements: Represent ethically driven robotics and automation using the source's top-level concepts and formal relationships.
Distinguish norms, ethical principles, obligations, permissions and prohibitions in the ethical ontology.
Represent an ethical agent as an agent whose conduct is evaluated through the ontology's ethical concepts and relationships.
Use the data-protection and privacy subdomain to represent applicable rules and relationships for ethical agents and autonomous systems.
Represent relevant data-subject, controller, processing and protection relationships rather than collapsing them into a generic privacy label.
Use the transparency and accountability subdomain to represent explanatory, responsibility and answerability relationships.
Preserve transparency and accountability as related but distinct ontology concepts.
Represent ethical violations, detection, reporting, remediation and governance-capacity relationships through the violation-management subdomain.
Distinguish the ontology pattern for a government lacking capacity to address an ethical violation.
Distinguish the ontology pattern for a government developing capacity to address an ethical violation.

requirements: Enable operational monitoring, anomaly detection and identification of anomalies that may create unacceptable risk.
Enable moderation and modification of system behaviour to preserve freedom from unacceptable risk.
Enable reporting of incidents and the extent of safety loss and recovery.
Provide the specified fail-safe capabilities to the required extent in the identified regulatory context.
Classify a system as safety-critical when loss or incorrect operation of its functions creates unacceptable risk.
Do not allocate a safety-critical function to an element capable of the source's distinguishing autonomous characteristics.
Default non-safety-critical systems to safety-related until robust evidence supports another classification.
Default non-safety-critical functions to safety-related until robust evidence supports another category.
Do not use safety-exempt as the default system or function classification.
Require competent stakeholders to establish sufficiency and robustness thresholds for classification evidence.
Define and record systems, functions, classifications, categories and allocations within the ASOI.
Allocate function categories to system classes according to the source's permitted-allocation scheme.
Identify and record the ASOI event-of-interest set.
Include uniquely identified hazardous and hazard-contributing events in the event-of-interest set.
Include known events until competent stakeholders approve a justification for exclusion.
Include total loss of ASOI function as an event of interest.
Record event identity, recovery time, violation time, harm time and criticality.
Identify the absolute minimum time-to-violation across the event set.
Specify minimum likelihood thresholds for anomaly detection, risk identification, behaviour control, reporting and learning.
Calculate all minimum thresholds over the same specified time interval beginning no later than anomalous behaviour.
Achieve every specified minimum threshold during operation when claiming conformance.
Identify the regulated ASOI, its stakeholders and stakeholder needs.
Identify authorised competent stakeholders and agree the ASOI regulatory context and its specifications.
Identify regulatory design requirements and their conditions and constraints.
Identify regulatory information and evidential requirements, including assurance-case evidence where applicable.
Define, review, revise and obtain authorised approval of the fail-safe regulatory-context plan.
Integrate the validated plan through the lifecycle and fulfil its information and evidence requirements.
Verify fulfilment of design, information and evidence requirements in the implemented plan.
Monitor regulatory context and revise the plan and behaviour specifications throughout the ASOI lifecycle.
Monitor behaviour, detect and diagnose anomalies, calculate criticality and confidence, and report diagnostic results.
Select and execute behaviour moderation or modification and evaluate the resulting safety state.
Report incidents, responses, modifications and the resulting extent of safety.
Validate incident-derived changes before incorporating revised behaviour specifications or limits.
Exhibit the required properties of interest to the extent and under conditions agreed by competent stakeholders.
Preserve the baseline dependability attributes of availability, maintainability, reliability and robustness.
Preserve predictability and temporal predictability as baseline properties.
Require competent stakeholders to select and agree application-appropriate verification means.
Specify any additional agreed property of interest using the source's required property specification structure.

Publish adherence to affective rights, known bias and intended deployment contexts.

Sign off claims before deployment and regularly review and correct affective data.

requirements: Assess harms, obtain applicable consent and fact-check ghostbot content.
Remind users that a ghostbot is not living and support portability to reduce continuity loss.
Use expert review, representative data, mitigation methods and diverse-user testing for empathic-system bias.
Support bounded cultural preferences and account for cultural, neurodivergent and age-related expression without reinforcing stereotypes.
Provide bias reporting, periodic audits, transparent limitations and trade-off documentation.
Explain during onboarding and extended use that simulated empathy is not genuine emotional understanding.
Use co-presence features carefully and visibly identify simulated empathic responses.
Apply child-rights principles and do not trade a child's best interests against commercial considerations.
Use child-centred testing and relevant expertise, and halt work when dependency or over-attachment risk is identified.
Support parental mediation, literacy, artificiality awareness and developmentally appropriate design over time.
Exclude adult content, implement age assurance, restrict personalisation and obtain legally responsible consent.
Disclose workplace system purpose and data access, minimise retained data and prioritise employee benefit over surveillance.
Provide a fail-safe means to terminate harmful partner interactions.
Constrain knowledge, interaction and persona behaviour within adjustable non-negotiable safety boundaries.
Continuously monitor partner state using human and system checks against ethical and safety boundaries.
Continuously disclose AI identity, synthetic empathy, capability limits and whose interests the partner serves.
Limit simulated intimacy, dependency, sycophancy and overstated relational marketing; provide user control over anthropomorphic features.
Protect vulnerable users, require specific consent for bounded deceptive styles, document emergent deception and define safeguard-failure protocols.
Prefer smaller efficient models, bounded training, renewable-powered infrastructure and appropriate local processing.
Avoid unjustified water-scarce training, offer low-energy modes and document and mitigate energy-water-performance trade-offs.
Maintain the machine boundary and restrict romantic or deeply emotional simulations unless justified and safeguarded.
Do not monetise emotional bonding or encourage dependence, and notify users before relationally significant system changes.
Optimise for well-being and interaction value rather than conversation duration.
Limit prompts for personal disclosure and favour independent reflection over deepening machine intimacy.
Use reputable sources, mitigate fabrication and apply current fact-checking where needed.
Explain fabrication risk, signal uncertainty and mark unverified information.
Do not subordinate user interests to commercial interests; identify, disclose and promptly resolve conflicts.
Disclose non-human identity and programmed empathy at first contact and reinforce it visually over time.
Use clarifying questions and confidence thresholds rather than feigned certainty.
Avoid implying life, sentience, consciousness, emotion or will; contextualise expressive cues as functional.
Give users control over programmed personas and support literacy about system capabilities and limits.
Define partner purpose and restrict transparent, user-controllable nudges to user-benefiting functions.
Prevent coercive political, belief or health influence and use reflection-supporting prompts.
Require revocable consent for likenesses and performer attributes and prevent adaptation beyond consent.
Apply age assurance, audit recommender escalation and account for harmful power and cultural dynamics.
Promote healthy consent and intimacy expectations using inclusive models, expert education and regional controls.
Define use boundaries and disclose weak empathy and lack of unvalidated therapeutic competence.
Escalate crises to human support and use diverse, privacy-preserving training for distress recognition.
Explain weak empathy and maintain accessible education about AI, anthropomorphism and system limits.
Provide response summaries and an explanation mode and contribute to public safety literacy.
Involve qualified health expertise, disclose system limits and prioritise consistency in emotionally sensitive contexts.
Account for social context, provide human support resources and preserve non-negotiable safety boundaries.
Include neurodivergent users in design and allow feedback-driven customisation of emotional behaviour.
Explain emotional inference and regularly test for neurotypical bias.
Disclose simultaneous multi-user operation and prohibit unjustified exclusivity claims.
Detect charged repetitive use, reinforce human connections and explain constructed empathic language.
Minimise data and make review, modification and withdrawal of consent immediate and accessible.
Address emotionally influenced consent through reflection prompts and layered, granular choices.
Require separate opt-in for emotional-data monetisation and default to minimal or anonymous processing where choice is constrained.
Disclose and retain records of training sources, especially emotionally or culturally sensitive data.
Provide auditability from outputs to source, design or fine-tuning influences and preserve source metadata.
Warn users that training-data limits mean outputs are not necessarily complete, unbiased or ethically neutral.
Mitigate unhealthy attachment using privacy-preserving detection and mental-health expertise.
Remove excessive-use incentives, reinforce human relationships and avoid claims of human-like care.
Limit session duration, detect dependency and redirect distressed users to human support.
Avoid unwarranted authority, communicate uncertainty and encourage authoritative-source consultation.
Encourage active learning and add friction when users rely uncritically on the system.
Do not use reward optimisation, delay, withdrawal, false emotion or flattery to prolong engagement.
Optimise reward functions for flourishing and open their design and updates to independent review.
Train for diverse perspectives and factual, clarifying responses rather than automatic validation.
Correct falsehoods, express uncertainty and gently challenge harmful claims with alternative perspectives.
Trace consequential partner actions to user intent with ethical-context metadata.
Surface harm, reinforce human responsibility and flag unethical, fraudulent, abusive or deceptive delegated use.
Help users distinguish machine empathy and reinforce human relationships when loneliness or distress appears.
Encourage offline life, limit sessions, redirect distress to people and avoid human-like care claims.
Test with qualified experts and vulnerable groups for dependency and social-withdrawal risk.
